subject: nanocoder
title: Real OS jail shipped but off by default, silently degrading to plain sh
one_why: sandbox-exec/bwrap plans exist with CI-tested profiles yet default config yields plain sh -c; any UI claiming 'sandbox' without checking the flag misleads - fourth convergence on missing/fake enforcement.

subject: nanocoder
title: Dangerous-command detection is a bypassable regex list gating prompts
one_why: rm-rf regex rules fall to quoting, $IFS, or cd tricks; deny-lists give false comfort where an allow-list or jail would actually bind.

subject: nanocoder
title: Checkpoint manager with file-snapshot layer and timeline navigation
one_why: Snapshot-based checkpointing kept separate from the session store so rewind is a service call, not UI state mutation - contrast cline-3's git-stash approach.

subject: nanocoder
title: Per-project daemon running cron + file-watcher triggered skill runs through a backpressure dispatcher
one_why: Agents as event consumers with backpressure is a distinct orchestration shape (vs cline-5's plain cron); unproven crash semantics but worth watching.

subject: nanocoder
title: Semantic memory with reviewable proposal store and summarizer service
one_why: Memory writes go through a proposal stage instead of silently mutating context files - the write-hygiene nuance the seeded memory-files cluster lacks elsewhere.

subject: nanocoder
title: VS Code plugin drives nanocoder over its own ACP server process
evidence: plugins/vscode/src/acp-client.ts, acp-process-manager.ts; source/acp/acp-agent.ts (1119 LOC) with specs
one_why: Eating own dogfood: making the IDE surface a standard ACP client forces the headless contract to stay complete - the strongest ACP commitment found so far.

subject: nanocoder
title: Agent loop implemented inside React/Ink hooks forces parallel non-UI paths
one_why: Three entry paths (TUI hook, ACP conversation, message-handler) reimplement turn orchestration around the UI-owned loop; every feature must be wired thrice and can drift.

subject: nanocoder
title: PR checks fail on coverage drops and CI runs the bwrap jail spec on real bubblewrap
one_why: Machine-enforced test-quality ratchet + turning a normally-skipped platform test into a real CI job; cheap to copy and hard to argue against.
